epic.title: epic-418-followon wave 2 — F2: MCP door adoption (#542) and friction capture (#541)
epic.intent_and_why: The MCP front door from F (#424) is built, merged and unused. Make agents drive through it, and make the door confess its own friction while they do. C (#421) does not launch until this is done: agents running the spine through the door is C's entry condition, set by the repo owner.

definition_of_done: Role spine instructions name the door's tools as the default path, CLI documented as the remaining fallback.
A real dispatched agent drove a real role spine to done through the door alone, measured from its own call record.
install_constellation.py ships and wires .mcp.json, so a fresh install gets the door.
The server's own rejections land in the run's episode through apply_episode_delta.py, and say so loudly when they cannot.
The identity trade is decided and the property given up is written down.

good_enough.mandatory_quality: Every gate closes on evidence produced AT that gate. No gate check that cannot lose.
good_enough.sufficient_evidence: Targeted automated tests plus the full suite at 0 failed; the acceptance claim measured from the driving agent's own call record, never server-side.
good_enough.appetite: One wave, one PR on epic-418/f2-mcp-adoption.

hard_constraints: The CLI door stays. F is additive. An edit that removes the CLI path fails g4a.
Never edit scripts/checklist_engine.py — the door wraps the engine and never re-implements it.
episodes/ is written only through apply_episode_delta.py with --store-root episodes.
An episode is a record, never read back as a rule.
Never write settings.json at user scope.
Do not reintroduce per-dispatch MCP config generation on identity grounds.
The main checkout /home/tommy/projects/constellation-skills is fenced read-only.
fixed_decisions: Gate order is g1 identity, g2 capture, g3 installer, g4 adoption+acceptance — the order is the point.
The acceptance numerator is the driving agent's own call record, never the server log.
A measured negative is a complete deliverable; an UNMEASURED condition is not a negative.
Identity may be bound to a container only at the granularity that container genuinely separates (g1).

current_wave.objective: Adopt the MCP door as the default path and instrument the door's own rejections.
exit_criteria: All five definition_of_done items evidenced, each at its own gate.

issues.title: Adopt the MCP door
issues.desired_outcome: Agents default to the door; a fresh install ships it; a real dispatched agent drives a real role spine to done through it alone.
issues.useful_now: It is C (#421)'s entry condition. C is written against whichever door delivers gate imperatives, so doing C against the CLI and porting afterwards is doing it twice.
issues.acceptance_or_falsification_evidence: The driving agent's own record.jsonl scored by F's archived instrument, requiring reached_done AND zero CLI engine invocations; plus the three adoption counts re-measured.
issues.implementation_latitude: Which role spines change and in what order; tool grouping; how the acceptance run is staged.
hard_constraints_no_gos: Removing or deprecating the CLI path.
local_unknowns: Whether an installed project-root dotfile should be default or opt-in — the installer has no precedent for writing one.

issues.title: Capture the door's own friction into the run's episode
issues.desired_outcome: The door records its own rejections, they reach the run's episode through apply_episode_delta.py, and it fails loud on every occurrence when they cannot.
issues.useful_now: The door absorbs rejections that used to be diagnosable in a transcript; without capture, adoption trades a visible defect for a silent one.
issues.acceptance_or_falsification_evidence: A seeded rejection scored by the instrument; a real episode written and read back under a nested work-id and verified with verify_episode_captured.py; N>=2 induced write failures producing N separate messages.
hard_constraints_no_gos: Do not extend the Mechanical allowlist or edit apply_episode_delta.py, episode_capture.py or docs/EPISODE_STORE.md — all outside this run's ownership.
Do not overload the engine's refusals counter or failed-commands.
Nothing written into episodes/ may be phrased as guidance for a future agent.

wave_forecast.outcome: C (#421) relocates gate-specific instructions into the spine, written against the door rather than the CLI.
wave_forecast.why_likely: The repo owner set 'agents running the spine through the door' as C's entry condition, and C's hard constraint is that the gate imperative rides tool results verbatim.
entry_conditions: F2 complete: role spine instructions default to the door and a real dispatched agent has driven a real role spine through it.

wave_evidence.claim: The launch order's framing of #541 - the door absorbs fumbles that would otherwise be diagnosable - describes the defect.
wave_evidence.expected: The door swallows rejections that reach no store.
wave_evidence.observed: Half true, and the false half would have wasted the gate. An ENGINE refusal through the door already moves the spine's refusals counter (0->1->2) and episode_capture composes that exact value into the Mechanical bin. Only the door's OWN _tool_error returns reach nothing: they short-circuit before run_engine, so they touch neither the counter nor the server's own call log. Measured on a nested work-id, 12/12 assertions.

wave_evidence.claim: A repo-wide suite postcondition is sufficient evidence that a gate's own work landed.
wave_evidence.expected: Suite green means the gate did its job.
wave_evidence.observed: False, and it was my own plan's defect. The suite was green before the run began, so all five integrate gates were satisfiable by a no-op diff plus an APPROVE. Every gate now closes on its own named test node first. A cold plan critic found this; the plan was revised before it froze.

wave_evidence.claim: A pin over a tool's declared inputSchema protects the door's confinement property.
wave_evidence.expected: No declared identity argument means the door cannot be redirected.
wave_evidence.observed: False. The g1 reviewer mutated the real door to honour an UNDECLARED spine_override key directly in call_tool's handler, touching no inputSchema, and all five pin tests stayed green. A pin over declarations is a pin over intentions. Two runtime tests were added and the reviewer's mutation now goes red; the recorded claim was narrowed to name both halves.

wave_evidence.claim: The identity defect is specific to the MCP door's env-binding.
wave_evidence.observed: False. The same shape appears independently in scripts/hooks/spine_rail.py (#549): its binding file IS keyed per agent, and session_view() then merges the per-agent key away. The harness shares the container and identity was put in the container, twice, neither seam aware of the other. g1's rule is therefore stated fleet-wide over container granularity rather than as an argument-passing fix - a form the hook seam forces, because it has no per-call argument for identity to ride on.

discrepancies.signal: map_orient.py returns DEGRADED-UNPARSEABLE against a map that is present, complete and fresh, and its verdict string carries the guess 'unfilled template?' which a Commander then reported one tier up as an observation.
discrepancies.affects: Every Commander in this epic runs map-DEGRADED and may repeat the same misreport.
discrepancies.evidence: map/INDEX.md is 23855 bytes over 132 modules / 4848 entities and tests/test_code_map.py::MapTreeFreshnessTests holds it byte-fresh. map_orient's ANCHOR_RE admits only hand-written packet vocabulary; a generated code map contains none by construction. #536 taught the probe where to look and not what it would find.
discrepancies.reason: Filed by the Admiral as #548. Not repaired inside a wave under measurement, per the launch order's cheap-fixes-are-routed rule.

discrepancies.signal: A Commander's own working notes at the repo root tripped tests/test_retirement_guard.py::test_canon_is_clean with six unapproved-store-mention violations.
discrepancies.affects: The launch order names notes-1.md as the working-notes convention, and prior runs put such files at the repo root.
discrepancies.evidence: The guard fires on any new SHIPPED site naming the episode store; a root-level run note discussing apply_episode_delta.py is exactly that shape. Resolved by moving the artifact into the run's own work area rather than by adding transient lines to a frozen approval census.
discrepancies.reason: The guard is correct and the note was the regression. Worth the Admiral knowing because the convention and the guard are in tension for any run that touches the episode store.

discrepancies.signal: Adding a test class silently staled map/INDEX.md, so the full suite was red for a reason unrelated to the gate's own work.
discrepancies.affects: Any gate in this epic that adds or removes entities.
discrepancies.evidence: tests.test_mcp_identity moved 36 -> 45 entities; MapTreeFreshnessTests failed until the map was rebuilt and committed.
discrepancies.reason: Mechanical and self-correcting once known. Recorded so a later gate recognises the failure instantly rather than diagnosing it again.

repo_state.map_status: Code map PRESENT and fresh: map/INDEX.md covers 132 modules / 4848 entities and tests/test_code_map.py::MapTreeFreshnessTests holds it byte-identical to a fresh build (it went red at g1 when the pin class was added and was rebuilt). map_orient.py still reports DEGRADED-UNPARSEABLE because its ANCHOR_RE admits only hand-written packet vocabulary and a generated code map carries none of it - the tool is what is broken, not the map. Filed as #548; discharged for this run with hash-pinned substitutes.
